t: Sumerian, the language of the city-states of southern Mesopotamia, is with Egyptian one of the two earliest written languages: its speakers developed cuneiform writing, at first to keep accounts, around 3200 BCE.

A language isolate unrelated to any other, it gave way as a spoken language to Akkadian around 2000 BCE, but remained the classical language of Mesopotamian religion and learning for nearly two thousand years.
Its literature, from the hymns of Enheduanna to the first stories of Gilgamesh, its law codes and its scribal schools make it one of the foundations of written civilisation.
dyk: The Sumerians counted in sixties, and through the astronomy of their Babylonian heirs their system survives in the sixty minutes of an hour and the 360 degrees of a circle.
ev: The first accounting tablets are written at Uruk in proto-cuneiform
The earliest Sumerian literary texts are copied at Shuruppak and Abu Salabikh
Enheduanna, high priestess at Ur and daughter of Sargon of Akkad, composes hymns in Sumerian
The law code of Ur-Nammu, the oldest known, is written in Sumerian
Babylonian scribal schools copy the classics of Sumerian literature, long after the language has ceased to be spoken
The last datable cuneiform tablet, an astronomical almanac, is written at Uruk
The scholar Jules Oppert gives the rediscovered language the name Sumerian

f.family: None known: a language isolate, related to no other known language
f.script: Cuneiform, developed in Sumer from around 3200 BCE; wedge-shaped signs pressed into clay
f.earliest: Accounting tablets from Uruk, around 3200 BCE; literary texts from about 2600 BCE
f.status: Extinct: spoken until around 2000 BCE, then written and studied as a classical language until the end of cuneiform in the 1st century CE
